description:
## Goal Ensure every public module is documented and `mix dialyzer` passes. This is the prerequisite for all guide work (I2–I6) — don't write guides for an API that is still undocumented. Deliverables: 1. All public modules have a meaningful `@moduledoc` (not "TODO") 2. All public functions have `@doc` and `@spec` 3. Internal/macro-generated modules marked `@moduledoc false` where appropriate 4. `mix dialyzer` exits 0 with no warnings 5. `mix docs` exits 0 and produces HTML in `doc/` 6. The top-level `Filament` module has an overview doc that orients new users ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## 0. Survey current state Before making any changes, run: ``` cd filament mix dialyzer 2>&1 | tail -30 mix docs 2>&1 | tail -20 ``` Record which warnings exist. Address each one individually. If dialyzer takes a long time on first run, that is expected (PLT build); subsequent runs are fast. --- ## 1. Public module inventory The following modules are public API — they must be fully documented: lib/filament.ex — top-level overview module lib/filament/component.ex — Filament.Component behaviour lib/filament/defcomponent.ex — defcomponent/prop macros lib/filament/sigil_f.ex — ~F sigil lib/filament/hooks.ex — use_state, use_observable, use_hold, use_memo, use_effect lib/filament/observable.ex — Filament.Observable behaviour lib/filament/observable/gen_server.ex — Filament.Observable.GenServer macro lib/filament/hold.ex — Filament.Hold behaviour lib/filament/hold/gen_server.ex — Filament.Hold.GenServer macro lib/filament/live_view.ex — Filament.LiveView macro The following are public but implementation-detail — mark with `@moduledoc false` if they are not currently intended to be user-facing, or add a minimal doc if they are needed for interop: lib/filament/fiber.ex — Filament.Fiber struct (mostly internal) lib/filament/fiber_tree.ex — Filament.FiberTree (mostly internal) lib/filament/reconciler.ex — Filament.Reconciler (mostly internal) lib/filament/renderer.ex — Filament.Renderer (mostly internal) lib/filament/render_context.ex — Filament.RenderContext (mostly internal) lib/filament/vnode.ex — Filament.VNode (internal) lib/filament/html_engine.ex — Filament.HTMLEngine (internal) lib/filament/event.ex — Filament.Event (internal or user-facing?) The following should be `@moduledoc false`: lib/filament/application.ex — Filament.Application (OTP supervisor) lib/filament/observable/subscriber.ex — Filament.Observable.Subscriber (already false) --- ## 2. Top-level Filament module FILE: lib/filament.ex Replace the existing placeholder moduledoc with a real overview: ```elixir defmodule Filament do @moduledoc """ Filament — a process-aware UI framework for Phoenix LiveView. Filament brings React-style component composition and hooks to LiveView, adding first-class support for observable domain state and resource holds. ## Core concepts **Components** are defined with `defcomponent`, declare typed `prop` attributes, and render HTML with the `~F` sigil (HEEx templates). defcomponent MyApp.Greeting do prop :name, :string, required: true def render(assigns) do ~F\"""

Hello, {@name}!

\""" end end **Hooks** run inside `render/1` and give components access to mutable state and external services: - `use_state/2` — local component state (re-renders on change) - `use_observable/3` — subscribe to an `Observable.GenServer` with an optional projection (only re-renders when the projected value changes) - `use_hold/3` — acquire a resource hold from a `Hold.GenServer`; released automatically if the LiveView process terminates - `use_memo/2` — memoised computation (recomputes only when deps change) - `use_effect/2` — side-effect with cleanup (run after render) **LiveView adapter** — use a Filament component tree as a LiveView: defmodule MyApp.MyLive do use Filament.LiveView def root_component, do: MyApp.RootComponent end ## Guides - "Getting Started" — first component, props, state, events, testing - "Observables" — Observable.GenServer, projections, change-or-bust - "Resource Holds" — Hold.GenServer, :DOWN lifecycle, out-of-stock UX - "Migration Guide" — converting LiveView assigns to Filament observables """ end ``` --- ## 3. Hooks module public API docs FILE: lib/filament/hooks.ex Ensure every public function (use_state, use_observable, use_hold, use_memo, use_effect, acquire_slot) has both `@doc` and `@spec`. The moduledoc should clarify the rules-of-hooks constraint and which functions are application-facing vs internal. Application-facing (users call these in render/1): use_state/1 and use_state/2 use_observable/1, use_observable/2, use_observable/3 use_hold/2 and use_hold/3 use_memo/2 use_effect/2 Internal (mark @doc false or omit from public docs): acquire_slot/1 (or equivalent low-level hook slot primitive) Example @spec additions: ```elixir @spec use_state(initial_value :: term()) :: {value :: term(), setter :: (term() -> :ok)} @spec use_state(default :: term(), key :: atom()) :: {value :: term(), setter :: (term() -> :ok)} @spec use_observable(server :: GenServer.server()) :: term() @spec use_observable(server :: GenServer.server(), request :: term()) :: term() @spec use_observable(server :: GenServer.server(), request :: term(), opts :: keyword()) :: term() @spec use_hold(server :: GenServer.server(), request :: term()) :: :uninitialized | {:held, token :: term(), item :: term()} | {:error, reason :: term()} @spec use_memo(compute_fn :: (-> term()), deps :: [term()]) :: term() @spec use_effect(effect_fn :: (-> cleanup :: (-> :ok) | nil), deps :: [term()]) :: :ok ``` Adapt these specs to match the actual implementations. If signatures differ, use what is actually in the file — do not change the implementation to match the spec. --- ## 4. Observable.GenServer macro docs FILE: lib/filament/observable/gen_server.ex The @moduledoc should explain what `use Filament.Observable.GenServer` injects: - handle_call({:filament_subscribe, ...}) — subscriber registration - handle_cast({:filament_unsubscribe, ...}) — subscriber removal - handle_info({:DOWN, ...}) — automatic subscriber cleanup on process death - notify_observers/1 — private function the user calls to push updates Include an example showing the minimal implementation: ```elixir defmodule MyApp.Counter do use Filament.Observable.GenServer def start_link(opts \\ []) do GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, 0, name: Keyword.get(opts, :name, __MODULE__)) end @impl Filament.Observable def handle_subscribe(_request, _subscriber, state) do {:ok, state, state} end @impl GenServer def handle_call(:increment, _from, count) do new_count = count + 1 notify_observers(new_count) {:reply, new_count, new_count} end end ``` --- ## 5. Hold.GenServer macro docs FILE: lib/filament/hold/gen_server.ex The @moduledoc should explain what `use Filament.Hold.GenServer` injects: - handle_call({:filament_acquire, ...}) — hold acquisition - handle_cast({:filament_release, ...}) — explicit release - handle_info({:DOWN, ...}) — automatic release on holder process death CRITICAL WARNING to include in @moduledoc: Do NOT use both `use Filament.Observable.GenServer` and `use Filament.Hold.GenServer` in the same module. Both inject `handle_info/2` for `{:DOWN, ref, :process, ...}` and the compiler will raise a duplicate clause error. If you need both capabilities in one server (e.g., Collaboration.DocumentServer), use only `Filament.Observable.GenServer` and implement lock/hold management manually in the server state. --- ## 6. mix.exs docs config — verify guide files match FILE: mix.exs The current `docs/0` function references: ```elixir extras: [ "CHANGELOG.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "guides/Getting Started.md", "guides/Observables.md", "guides/Resource Holds.md", "guides/Migration Guide.md" ] ``` All four guide stubs already exist under `guides/`. I2–I4 and I6 will fill them in. Verify that `mix docs` picks them up correctly by running `mix docs` after this ticket and checking that the extras appear in `doc/index.html`. If the logo reference (`logo: ".tmp/logo.png"`) causes a warning (file missing), either remove it or replace with a real logo. Do not let a missing logo block `mix docs`. Add a `groups_for_modules` to organize the generated API docs by category: ```elixir defp docs do [ main: "Filament", logo: ".tmp/logo.png", # remove if not present extras: [ "CHANGELOG.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "guides/Getting Started.md", "guides/Observables.md", "guides/Resource Holds.md", "guides/Migration Guide.md" ], groups_for_modules: [ "Components": [Filament.Component, Filament.Defcomponent, Filament.SigilF], "Hooks": [Filament.Hooks], "Observables": [Filament.Observable, Filament.Observable.GenServer], "Holds": [Filament.Hold, Filament.Hold.GenServer], "LiveView": [Filament.LiveView], "Internals": [ Filament.Fiber, Filament.FiberTree, Filament.Reconciler, Filament.Renderer, Filament.RenderContext ] ] ] end ``` Adjust module names to match what actually compiles. Remove modules from the list if they don't exist or are marked `@moduledoc false`. --- ## 7. Dialyzer Run `mix dialyzer` and fix all warnings. Common categories: - Type mismatch in callback returns - Missing @spec on public functions that dialyzer infers for - Unreachable clauses Do NOT silence warnings with `@dialyzer` annotations unless the warning is a known false positive from a macro expansion. If a warning looks real, fix the underlying code. --- ## 8. Acceptance criteria - [ ] `mix dialyzer` exits 0 with no warnings - [ ] `mix docs` exits 0 and produces `doc/index.html` - [ ] `doc/index.html` contains links to all four guide pages - [ ] All public modules in the inventory (section 1) have a non-placeholder `@moduledoc` - [ ] `Filament.Hooks` public functions all have `@doc` and `@spec` - [ ] `Filament.Observable.GenServer` @moduledoc includes the :DOWN-conflict warning - [ ] Full test suite passes: `mix test`
title: I1: HexDocs foundation — complete @moduledoc/@doc/@spec, dialyzer clean, mix docs generates
